algebra.nu_series_at_0: g_N^(-1/2) (a Puiseux series: no Taylor series exists)

checks.name: the law is the elimination of u: g_N = g^2/(g+a0) = u^2/(a0(1-u/a0))
checks.reading: g = K W'(u) = u/(1-u/a0) is the saturating-log force; g_N = g-u is A33 section 5's first integral. The two combine to the law (A33 K3). Rewritten in u = K|P| -- the P sector's OWN field -- the law says something the record has not used: g_N is QUADRATIC in the P field

checks.name: the response in closed form: nu = g/g_N = a0/u exactly
checks.reading: the whole content of the law is that the boost is the ratio a0/u. Nothing else -- no k, no H, no delta. u is the P field. So 'which field is g_N' is the same question as 'what sets u', and at the level of the algebra the only available answer is: the source's own field

checks.name: g_N has NO linear term in u: dg_N/du|_0 = 0, d2g_N/du2|_0 = 2/a0
checks.reading: *** The Newtonian field is QUADRATIC in the P field. ***  A first-order perturbation of P produces a SECOND-order g_N, so the modification cannot appear at first order in the density contrast. It is not that the effect is small; it is that it is absent at the order where linear growth is defined

checks.name: the inverse is a SQUARE ROOT: u = sqrt(a0 g_N); nu = sqrt(a0/g_N) is non-analytic at g_N = 0
checks.threshold: u^2/(a0 g_N) -> 1; nu' ~ g_N^(-1/2) (a Puiseux series: no Taylor series exists)
checks.reading: the law has a branch point at zero field: nu -> infinity as g_N -> 0 and nu has no Taylor series there. Hence there is NO regime in which the response is 1 + O(field): at high field it is 1 + (a0/g_N)^2 (A40 K6, quadratic), at low field it is sqrt(a0/g_N) (a square root). The two ends do not meet in a linear term

checks.name: for a gradient mode the (D.P)^2 and F^2 terms combine exactly into lap^2(dP_i)
checks.reading: the longitudinal piece of the F^2 operator cancels the (D.P)^2 operator identically. So the P sector's spatial operator is gamma lap^2: an ELLIPTIC CONSTRAINT with stiffness gamma = K L*^2/2, not a propagating scalar. That is why P is a slave at cosmological scales -- and it is the term A33 section 7.4 records as mis-transcribed in A3

checks.name: the coefficient multiplying grad(delta Phi) is 1/K to 1e-12 at cosmological k
checks.value: 1/(1+(k lambda_P)^2) - 1 = -1.308e-12 at k = 0.1 h/Mpc (k lambda_P = 1.14e-06); kinetic term (eta/K)H^2 = 1.5e-17
checks.reading: *** THE COEFFICIENT IS 1. ***  delta P_i = d_i(delta Phi)/K exactly, in the quasi-static sub-horizon limit. The P field is not an independent degree of freedom: it is the gradient of the potential, with unit coefficient. A 17 pc stiffness is 1e-12 of the cosmological scales and the Compton term is 1e-17, so no k or omega dependence survives

checks.name: eliminating psi gives G_eff/G = 1 + 1/(k lambda_P)^2 -> DIVERGENT: no linear Newtonian limit
checks.value: Phi = -K*rho*(K + gamma*k**2)/(gamma*k**4); G_eff/G = K/(gamma*k**2) + 1 = 7.64e+11 at k = 0.1 h/Mpc
checks.reading: *** THE LINEAR ORDER OF THE ACTION HAS NO FINITE SOLUTION. ***  The charge delta d = lap^2(delta Phi)/K is a copy of the Poisson source with coefficient 1, so A22's (4)+(6) give lap^2(Phi) = K rho (1 + K/(gamma k^2)): an anti-screened G_eff of 1/(k lambda_P)^2 = 7.6e11 at 0.1 h/Mpc. The potential runs away as k^-4, so the linearised system is not a truncation of any solution -- exactly the 'zero-field k^2 runaway' A40 cites (FP22 B0-B4), now with its coefficient. There is no linear growth equation: not 'LCDM', not 'modified'

checks.name: the linear branch is the deep-MOND endpoint: g_N/g = (k lambda_P)^2 -> 0, g -> a0 (k lambda_P)^2
checks.reading: at linear order u = g to 1e-12 and g_N/g = (k lambda_P)^2: the P field carries essentially the whole field and the Newtonian field vanishes. Combined with the law (g_N = u^2/a0) the only field the linear system admits is g = a0 (k lambda_P)^2 ~ 1.5e-22 m/s^2 -- i.e. zero. Linearising about P = 0 is an expansion about the deep-MOND endpoint, not about GR

checks.name: the linear solution is NOT the delta->0 limit: u_exact/u_linear = sqrt(a0/g_N) = 22
checks.value: ratio at the 8 h^-1 Mpc field = 22.47; at 0.1 a0 = 3.16; at 1 a0 = 1.00
checks.threshold: ratio > 10 (the linear solution is the wrong branch)
checks.reading: the exact small-source solution has u = sqrt(a0 g_N), which is LARGER than g_N and scales as delta^(1/2), not delta. The linearised system (u = g) and the exact solution (u = sqrt(a0 g_N)) are different branches; the map between them is singular at delta = 0. So 'the modification is a small perturbation of GR' is not a statement this action can make

checks.name: the first nonzero correction is O(g_N/a0) = 0.2%: the a0 effect enters at SECOND order
checks.reading: because g_N = u^2/a0 + u^3/a0^2, the P sector's contribution to the potential at second order is (grad dPhi)^2/a0, i.e. a fraction g_N/a0 = 0.21% of the first-order Newtonian field at the 8 h^-1 Mpc peak and 0.18% at 100 Mpc (the smoothed field is nearly flat past its peak). That is the entire a0 imprint on linear growth: below every quoted error bar (sigma8 would move by < 0.2%)

checks.name: the integrator reproduces the exact growing mode on BOTH backgrounds
checks.value: flat LCDM: D(1) = 0.788559 vs integral 0.788559, f(0) = 0.52833; theory bg (G_eff=1): D(1) = 0.739201 vs integral 0.739201
checks.reading: the solver is A40's, re-implemented: flat LCDM at Omega_m = 0.3163 gives D(1) = 0.7886, f(0) = 0.5283; on the theory's E^2 = 1 + Omega_m a^-3 the same integral gives 0.7392. Every sigma8 below is 0.811 * D(1)/0.7886 (A40's anchor)

checks.name: branch (a), the cosmic reference field cH: reproduces A40's sigma8 = 0.7619
checks.reading: A40's branch (a) is reproduced. Note what it is: g_ref = cH is an acceleration the ACTION does not contain -- no term in A33 section 1 has an H in it. It is a posit, and this check certifies only that the number is reproducible

checks.name: branch (b), the perturbation's own rms field: reproduces A40's sigma8 = 2.267 (excluded)
checks.reading: A40's branch (b) is reproduced: applying the exact law pointwise to the perturbation's own field drives sigma8 to 2.267. This is the RESUMMED law (the sqrt branch), not a linearisation -- K1-K9 prove the latter does not exist

checks.name: the adopted (inert) branch: G_eff = 1 at every linear scale, sigma8 and f(z)
checks.reading: with the P sector left at its FRW value the theory grows exactly as GR on its own background: sigma8(0) = 0.760, 6.3% below Planck-2018's 0.811. The background does the suppressing: H(0) = 77.3 and Omega_m(a=1) = 0.2403 give D(1) = 0.7392 vs LCDM's 0.7886

checks.name: the threshold scan is monotone and brackets the target: delta_c(0.832) is well defined
checks.reading: the threshold reading sweeps from the full pointwise law at delta_c -> 0 (sigma8 = 3.35: worse than A40's 2.267, because RESP ~ delta^-1/2 diverges as delta -> 0 and the 8/h Mpc mode starts from zero) to the inert branch at delta_c -> infinity. It has one free parameter and no derivation

checks.name: the delta_c that reproduces Planck's sigma8 is BELOW the nonlinear scale
checks.value: delta_c(0.832) = 0.677;  delta = 1 at 8/h Mpc;  delta_collapse = 1.686;  ratio = 0.40;  sigma8 at delta_c = 1.686: 0.7602
checks.reading: *** the bound-system reading cannot deliver sigma8 = 0.832. ***  To reach Planck the modification must switch on in the QUASI-LINEAR regime, at delta ~ 0.5-0.8, a factor 2-3 below the collapse threshold. At the bound-system scale (delta_c = 1.686) the sigma8 mode never triggers it and the prediction is the inert 0.760, 6.3% low. So 'the law acts only in bound systems' is consistent with the data but not preferred by them

checks.name: at delta_c = 1.686 the modification never fires for the sigma8 mode: sigma8 = inert
checks.reading: the 8/h Mpc sphere reaches delta = 0.76 at z = 0, so a threshold at 1.686 is never crossed and the growth is exactly the inert one. The reading is self-consistent and empty: it converts the fork into a nonlinear-scale statement with no linear signature

checks.name: the transfer function gives the Planck shape: k_NL and sigma(R) where they should be
checks.value: sigma(1 Mpc) = 3.53, sigma(10 Mpc) = 0.932, sigma(100 Mpc) = 0.0717, k_NL = 0.224 h/Mpc; monotone = True
checks.threshold: 3 < sigma(1 Mpc) < 8; 0.05 < sigma(100 Mpc) < 0.15; 0.12 < k_NL < 0.35 h/Mpc; monotone
checks.reading: EH98 no-wiggle (zero-baryon), n_s = 0.965, amplitude fixed by the same Planck anchor A40 uses. k_NL = 0.22 h/Mpc is the standard Planck value, which calibrates the shape. The shape is only needed at the few-% level: the conclusion below is a factor 479

checks.name: NO linear scale reaches a0: the filter scale R(a0) does not exist in the linear field
checks.value: max g_R/a0 = 0.0021 at R = 21.5 Mpc; shortfall = 479x
checks.reading: *** a0 is not a cosmic acceleration. ***  The rms smoothed linear field peaks at R ~ 20 Mpc at 0.21% of a0; at every other scale it is smaller (0.18% even at 100 Mpc, because sigma(R) R is almost flat past the turnover). There is no R at which 'the mean smoothed field equals a0' in the linear universe. Whatever sets the MOND transition in cosmology, it is not a linear smoothing of the density field

checks.name: the filter on the LINEAR field does not rescue growth: G_eff ~ 11-15 at every R
checks.value: G_eff/G in [11.5, 291.1] for R in [1 kpc, 10 Gpc] -> sigma8 ~ 2.27
checks.reading: smoothing a linear mode does not reduce its field: a 15 kpc filter applied to a 100 Mpc mode returns the mode's own field. So the filtered reading at linear scales IS branch (b); the filter changes nothing. This is the check that kills the naive 'environmental' rescue of linear growth

checks.name: R(a0) exists only in the NONLINEAR field, at galaxy radii: k(a0) ~ 1e2 h/Mpc
checks.value: R(a0) = 12883 pc for v_c = 150 km/s (range 1431-51532 pc); k(a0) = 115 h/Mpc
checks.reading: the a0 transition happens where the field really is a0, and that is inside galaxies: R(a0) = 2 sigma^2/a0 = 1.4-52 kpc for v_c = 50-300 km/s. Hence k(a0) = 29-1037 h/Mpc, two to four decades above every linear scale (k <~ 0.2 h/Mpc). The modification is a sub-grid, object-by-object effect; the PM engine CFG960 applies it exactly this way (y = G M_b(<r)/r^2 at the local r)

checks.name: the filtered reading's growth prediction: G_eff = 1 on all linear scales
checks.reading: the filtered and the inert branch coincide: both are GR on the theory's background, because the only places the filtered field reaches a0 are k ~ 1e2 h/Mpc, where the linear growth equation is not the right description anyway. sigma8 = 0.760, and f(z) is the LCDM shape on the theory's background

checks.name: branch (b) is BLUE (G_eff varies 30% across the linear range); the filtered reading is not
checks.reading: the scale dependence is the cleanest discriminator: branch (b) boosts 5 h^-1 Mpc 60% more than 20 h^-1 Mpc; the filtered and inert readings are exactly scale-free. Measuring f sigma8 at two k at one z decides it, and so does the shape of P(k) at 0.05-0.3 h/Mpc

checks.name: the amplitude discriminator: branch (b) over-produces 1e15 Msun clusters by ~1e3
checks.reading: sigma8 = 2.267 is not a 6% effect: with sigma(M) ~ 0.49 sigma8, exp(-delta_c^2/2sigma^2) changes by ~3 orders of magnitude at the cluster scale. Branch (b) is excluded by cluster counts alone, independently of any growth-rate measurement

checks.name: the prediction is distinguishable from LCDM through the BACKGROUND, not through a0
checks.reading: on the literal beta = 0 background the growth rate is 14% below LCDM's at z = 0 and sigma8 is 6.3% low. That is the theory's real growth signature -- a background effect (H(0) = 77.3, Omega_m(a=1) = 0.2403), not an a0 effect. Testable with DESI DR2 at z < 0.6 where the errors are 1-2%
